response.sql:
WITH fee_order_join AS (
  SELECT 
    f.orderslink,
    o.dealedge,
    (f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS net_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    dealedge,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS group_avg_net_fee_rate,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM fee_order_join
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
),
side_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    dealedge,
    AVG(group_avg_net_fee_rate) AS side_avg
  FROM group_stats
  GROUP BY dealedge
)
SELECT 
  gs.orderslink,
  gs.dealedge,
  gs.group_avg_net_fee_rate,
  gs.record_count,
  (gs.group_avg_net_fee_rate - sa.side_avg) AS difference
FROM group_stats gs
JOIN side_averages sa ON gs.dealedge = sa.dealedge
WHERE gs.group_avg_net_fee_rate > sa.side_avg
ORDER BY (gs.group_avg_net_fee_rate - sa.side_avg) DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Record count: COUNT(*) counts all fee records in each (orderslink, dealedge) group, including those where net_fee_rate is NULL. The average net_fee_rate is computed only from non-NULL values (standard SQL AVG behavior).
Groups with NULL average (all their net_fee_rates are NULL) are excluded from the result because the WHERE clause filters on strict inequality, treating NULL comparisons as false.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only records with non-NULL net_fee_rate (i.e., COUNT(net_fee_rate) instead of COUNT(*)), so the reported record count reflects the sample size used for the group average.
